# PENICILLIN DESENSITIZATION PROTOCOL

Pharmacy Service must be involved. Contact satellite pharmacist at ext. 2040 or menu 648-6746. Infectious Diseases Consult strongly recommended.

When penicillin is the drug of choice for an infectious disease in a patient with Type I penicillin allergy, one option is to desensitize the patient.

Severe reactions cannot be predicted accurately with skin testing in the clinical setting.

# Penicillin Desensitization

Perform in an ICU or similar setting.

Discontinue all beta-adrenergic antagonists.

Have IV line in place and EKG and spirometer ready.

Once desensitization has been accomplished, therapy with this drug must not lapse or the risk of allergic reactions increases.

A history of Stevens Johnson syndrome, exfoliative dermatitis, or erythroderma are nearly absolute contraindications to desensitization.

---

# ORAL ROUTE

---

Oral route is preferred if oral preparation is available and GI tract is functional. 1/3 of patients will develop transient reaction, usually mild.

# [Step, 15 minute intervals] concentration, volume

[1] 0.5mg/ml, 0.1ml

[2] 0.5mg/ml, 0.2ml

[3] 0.5mg/ml, 0.4ml

[4] 0.5mg/ml, 0.8ml

[5] 0.5mg/ml, 1.6ml

[6] 0.5mg/ml, 3.2ml

[7] 0.5mg/ml, 6.4ml

[8] 5mg/ml, 1.2ml

[9] 5mg/ml, 2.4ml

[10] 5mg/ml, 4.8ml

[11] 50mg/ml, 1ml

[12] 50mg/ml, 2ml

[13] 50mg/ml, 4ml

[14] 50mg/ml, 8ml

After step 14, observe 30 minutes. If no reaction, give 1 gm IV.

# PARENTERAL ROUTE

---

# [Step, 15 minute intervals] concentration, volume

[1] 0.1mg/ml, 0.1ml

[2] 0.1mg/ml, 0.2ml

[3] 0.1mg/ml, 0.4ml

[4] 0.1mg/ml, 0.8ml

[5] 1mg/ml, 0.16ml

[6] 1mg/ml, 0.32ml

[7] 1mg/ml, 0.64ml

[8] 10mg/ml, 0.12ml

[9] 10mg/ml, 0.24ml

[10] 10mg/ml, 0.48ml

[11] 100mg/ml, 0.1ml

[12] 100mg/ml, 0.2ml

[13] 100mg/ml, 0.4ml

[14] 100mg/ml, 0.8ml

[15] 1000mg/ml, 0.16ml

[16] 1000mg/ml, 0.32ml

[17] 1000mg/ml, 0.64ml

After step 17, observe 30 minutes. If no reaction, give 1 gm IV.
